title: The run log carries what the agent actually did
description:
The panel cannot show a Read differently from a Bash because nothing on the wire says which one it was. `LogLine` in packages/schema/src/wire.ts is `{ kind, text }` with six kinds — started, text, tool, result, raw, answer — and the tool's name is flattened into the prose.

Worse, in the claude adapter in packages/core/src/hosts.ts: one `assistant` event maps its `content` parts through a single `.map()`, joins whatever survives with ` · `, and stamps the whole thing `tool` if any part was a tool_use. So the agent's sentence to the human and the name of the tool it called land on one line under one kind. And `part.type === 'thinking'` is matched by nothing, so thinking is dropped before it ever reaches a screen — there is no spinner to build until this changes.

The work: give a line somewhere to say which tool, and give thinking a kind of its own. Then split the assistant mapping so one event can produce several lines — the prose as its own line, each tool call as its own line — rather than one joined string. The other three adapters (codex `command_execution`, opencode `tool_use`, cursor `tool_call`) each already know the tool's name at the point they build the line and throw it away the same way; carry it through in all four.

Check before widening the type: the exported-surface ratchet, and whether the board's schema version covers wire types at all — `LogLine` is what a screen is sent, not a record on the board branch, and a version bump that nothing reads is noise. Update the adapter tests in the same node; this is a type and its producers, which do not land separately.
